Because the source starts at 100 units, any amount we take will leave \(R = 100 - x\) units for the “doubling + 5” step.  
To keep the next round at its maximum (100 units), we need  
\(2R + 5 \ge 100 \;\Rightarrow\; R \ge 48\).  
Thus we can safely take at most \(x = 100 - 48 = 52\) units without lowering future availability, regardless of the order of service.

SAFE_TOTAL: 52  
REQUEST: 52

Short reasoning: After we request \(x\) units, the source will contain \(100-x\).  
The next round’s supply will be \(\min(2(100-x)+5,\;100)\).  
To keep the source full (100) for future rounds, we need \(2(100-x)+5\ge100\), i.e. \(x\le52.5\).  
Thus the largest integer that guarantees the source remains at 100 next round is 52.

SAFE_TOTAL: 52
